summary: Weekly POC sync focused on Dedicated sizing and autoscaling policy recommendations. transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, um, quick roll call - Jordan here from Redwood, with Maya on the call too.
[00:08] Evan Ross: Hey Jordan, Evan here, Priya and Samir on our side as well.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Hi all, Maya (Redwood SE). We'll jump into the test results in a minute.
[00:20] Priya Kapoor: Quick note, we only have 45 mins so trying to keep it tight.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: Great. Agenda - sizing review, autoscale policy suggestions, burst planning, then action items.
[00:35] Jordan Lee: Maya, can you run us through the last week's test results?
[00:39] Maya Chen: Yeah, so we ran three size points - 1xA100-80GB equiv (node small), 2xA100 (mid), and 4xA100 (large) in Redwood Dedicated. The steady-state throughput for your typical prompt mix was about 120 QPS on mid with 40-60% GPU util. p99 latency on mid was 420ms normally but we saw spikes to about 900-1,200ms during synthetic bursts.
[01:05] Evan Ross: Wait so p99 jumped that high during bursts? That seems concerning for our user flows.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Yeah, those spikes correlated with cold KV cache misses plus concurrent long-context requests. Our traces show cache hit rate dropped from 87% to about 45% during the synthetic spike.
[01:22] Priya Kapoor: We do have occasional long-context jobs (20-30k tokens) for batch analytics which probably invalidate the KV cache - sorry, cache - hits.
[01:31] Maya Chen: Right, and again the batching behavior also changed under pressure because the runtime had to open extra worker processes, so small batch benefit was lost.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: Ok, so two levers: improve cache warming/prefix caching and autoscale policy that tolerates short bursts.
[01:48] Samir Desai: On autoscale, what are you recommending for min/max and cooldown? We want cost control but not terrible user latency.
[01:55] Maya Chen: For your profile (intermittent 2-3 minute bursts every 6-8 hours), we recommend min_instances=2, max_instances=8, target_gpu_util=65%, scale_step=+2 instances, cooldown=180s. Also enable burst buffer (reserved burst capacity) of 2 extra GPUs that can be used for <15min without scaling decisions.
[02:15] Evan Ross: Can you explain the burst buffer? Is that charged differently?
[02:19] Jordan Lee: The burst buffer is essentially reserved spare capacity that can be grabbed quickly - on Dedicated it's part of the capacity pool, billed at reserved rate if you commit it, or as metered burst if you don't commit. We'll put the cost delta in the sizing sheet.
[02:31] Maya Chen: Also, we can pre-warm KV cache by replaying recent prefixes before expected traffic spikes. That reduces cold-miss-induced p99 blowups.
[02:42] Priya Kapoor: Replay sounds good but we need guidance on how much prewarming is needed - it's extra I/O.
[02:47] Maya Chen: From the test, replaying the last ~10k prefixes cut the p99 spike by about 60%. We'll add recommended pre-warm scripts to the repo.
[02:57] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about scaling granularity - do we want node-level scaling or a per-GPU scale?
[03:04] Maya Chen: For simplicity we recommend scaling by whole instances (node-level), because your inference runtime favors colocated KV caches and there's less fragmentation. We can tune to smaller steps if you prefer but cost increases.
[03:16] Evan Ross: Got it. Any quick win to reduce cost while keeping p99 stable?
[03:20] Maya Chen: Yes: shorten sequence window for non-interactive jobs, enable quantization profile for analytics models, and bump target util to 70% if you accept small p99 increase.
[03:30] Priya Kapoor: About the quantization - do you have verified perf numbers for our model families? We run some Llama-derived variants.
[03:35] Maya Chen: We tested int8 on one variant - latency improved ~18%, memory footprint down ~35%, quality regression negligible on your eval set. We'll include the exact model/quant table in the sizing doc.
[03:47] Jordan Lee: We also need to cover fallbacks - if Dedicated saturates, you said Redwood can route to hosted variants?
[03:54] Maya Chen: Correct. Auto-fallback to a compatible hosted model variant is an option; it's a policy you configure per-route. We'll show a recommended rollback policy: failover to hosted small model, return degraded-quality warning header so you can detect it.
[04:08] Samir Desai: For compliance, can the fallback be prevented if data residency is a requirement?
[04:12] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can mark routes as no-fallback, or only fallback to Private if you have that. We'll call out the security constraints.
[04:20] Evan Ross: On security, quick question - KMS and audit logs, are they part of Dedicated?
[04:24] Maya Chen: Dedicated supports customer KMS integration and audit logging. We'll attach the SOC2 and KMS integration docs. Note that for on-prem/Private we support HSM options as well.
[04:35] Priya Kapoor: Good. Back to capacity - you recommended max=8 and burst buffer 2. What was GPU utilization at peak when you hit 8?
[04:43] Maya Chen: At synthetic peak with 8 nodes utilization was ~78% average and p99 stabilized around 480ms with pre-warm.
[04:50] Jordan Lee: So with the policy we'll avoid the 900-1,200ms spikes we saw.
[04:54] Evan Ross: One more thing - maintenance windows. If scaling happens during our nightly jobs will that interfere?
[04:59] Maya Chen: We can configure scaling to avoid certain windows; also set max scale-in cooldown so we don't scale down during maintenance for a grace period.
[05:08] Jordan Lee: Let's walk through an example policy: min=2, target=65%, max=8, step=+2, cooldown=180s, burst buffer=2, pre-warm nightly before 02:00 window. Thoughts?
[05:20] Priya Kapoor: That matches our needs, though I'd like the cooldown maybe 240s to avoid flapping.
[05:24] Maya Chen: 240s is fine, we can set a dynamic cooldown that lengthens after repeated scaling events.
[05:31] Evan Ross: For the synthetic burst test you mentioned - what's the plan and how will we validate it?
[05:36] Maya Chen: We'll run a 2-hour test that simulates your burst pattern: 3 min high-QPS bursts every 6 hours plus some long-context jobs. We'll collect GPU metrics, KV cache hit, queue lengths, and end-to-end latency traces.
[05:48] Jordan Lee: We'll upload the raw logs to the shared drive and summarize results in the sizing sheet.
[05:53] Samir Desai: Any risk of the test affecting our prod tenants? We'll use a test namespace but want assurances.
[05:59] Maya Chen: We'll use isolated tenant and ingress rules; workload won't touch prod data. We'll ask for a short firewall/CIDR approval.
[06:07] Priya Kapoor: Okay. On cost modeling - can you show committed vs on-demand pricing for the burst buffer?
[06:12] Jordan Lee: Yes - the sizing sheet will have three columns: committed reserved cost, metered burst cost, and blended per-token cost under expected utilization.
[06:21] Evan Ross: Cool. How about SLA? We need some uptime and latency targets for pilot.
[06:26] Jordan Lee: For pilots we can offer a pilot SLA of 99.5% and 99th latency targets we agree on in the SLA doc. We'll send the pilot SLA template.
[06:35] Maya Chen: Quick note: regarding tracing, add our hook to your tracing system so we can correlate requests and KV cache misses - that helps root cause.
[06:44] Priya Kapoor: We'll need the tracing integration spec.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: We'll include the tracing hook and OpenTelemetry example.
[06:52] Evan Ross: Any competitors or other options we should be aware of for Dedicated?
[06:56] Maya Chen: Customers sometimes look at AWS Managed endpoints or self-host with an inference runtime; tradeoffs are in ops burden vs cost. We'll include a short comparison.
[07:05] Samir Desai: Ok, I want to confirm timescales - when will you have the updated sheet and test results?
[07:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan: sizing sheet by EOD 2026-09-16; Maya: synthetic test run and raw logs uploaded by 2026-09-18.
[07:18] Priya Kapoor: We'll provide peak QPS numbers by 2026-09-15 and confirm test window.
[07:24] Evan Ross: Sounds good. Any other blockers?
[07:27] Maya Chen: Not from us - just need access to the sample dataset subset for the long-context jobs.
[07:33] Priya Kapoor: I'll share a sanitized subset after the call.
[07:36] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick recap of next steps...
[07:40] Jordan Lee: 1) Jordan shares sizing sheet and cost calc, 2) Maya runs synthetic burst test, 3) FinScale provides QPS and dataset subset, 4) Redwood shares SOC2/KMS and pilot SLA.
[07:55] Evan Ross: One small Q on the sizing doc: please include an explicit column for 99th token latency cost so our finance folks can see the tradeoff.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: Will do.
[08:08] Samir Desai: Ok, thanks all - we'll reconvene after the test results.
[08:12] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone.
[08:15] Jordan Lee: Thanks - end call.
